question_text: In a laboratory creep experiment at $1,000^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, a steady-state creep rate of $5 \times 10^{-1} \%$ per hour is obtained in a metal alloy. The creep mechanism for this alloy is known to be dislocation climb with an activation energy of $200 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$. Predict the creep rate at a service temperature of $600^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. (Assume that the laboratory experiment duplicated the service stress.)The unit of the answer is % per hour.
response:
The steady-state creep rate follows an Arrhenius relationship:

$$\dot{\varepsilon} = A\exp\!\left(-\frac{Q}{RT}\right)$$

With the same stress, the pre-exponential factor $A$ is unchanged, so

$$\frac{\dot{\varepsilon}_2}{\dot{\varepsilon}_1}=\exp\!\left[-\frac{Q}{R}\!\left(\frac{1}{T_2}-\frac{1}{T_1}\right)\right]$$

Using $T_1=1273\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_2=873\ \mathrm{K}$, $Q=200{,}000\ \mathrm{J/mol}$, $R=8.314\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$, and $\dot{\varepsilon}_1=5\times10^{-1}\ \%/ \mathrm{hr}$:

$$\dot{\varepsilon}_2 = 0.5\cdot\exp\!\left[-\frac{200000}{8.314}\!\left(\frac{1}{873}-\frac{1}{1273}\right)\right]\approx 8.68\times10^{-5}\ \%/ \mathrm{hr}$$

$$\boxed{8.68\times10^{-5}}$$
